title: Sweet Season
content: Rejoice: NYT Cooking’s holiday cookie extravaganza has returned.

title: Like Trump, Benjamin Franklin Sought to Annex Canada
content: A book revives the largely forgotten story of how one of America’s most famous founding fathers tried to make Canada a part of his new nation.

title: Scientists Are Measuring Ocean Currents in Hopes of Charting AMOC’s Future
content: Scientists fear warming is driving a collapse in the ocean currents that shape climate far and wide. The ice-choked waters off Greenland might hold the key.

title: Trump’s Security Strategy Focuses on Profit, Not Spreading Democracy
content: President Trump’s new National Security Strategy describes a country that is focused on doing business and reducing migration while avoiding passing judgment on authoritarians.

title: Man Who Swallowed Stolen Fabergé Egg Passes It Naturally, Police Say
content: The man ingested the egg locket at a jewelry store in New Zealand last week, according to the authorities.

title: ICE Arrests Harvard Professor Charged for Shooting a Pellet Gun
content: Carlos Portugal Gouvea, a visiting law professor from Brazil, said he would leave the country rather than be deported, according to federal officials. He was arrested after firing a pellet gun near a synagogue.

title: Trump Wants Maduro to Go. Here’s Who Could Replace Him in Venezuela.
content: Several senior Venezuelan officials and opposition politicians would have a claim to power in a transition, but all would face difficulties.

title: Air Traffic Control Issue Briefly Grounds Flights at Edinburgh Airport
content: The airport, Scotland’s busiest, said it had experienced a technical problem with its air traffic control provider. An hour later, flights had resumed.

title: How the U.S. Focus on Fentanyl Helped Fuel the Cocaine Trade’s Resurgence
content: Across Latin America, cocaine trafficking has surged as Washington has prioritized combating fentanyl. Times reporters traveled to Ecuador to see how criminal groups are wreaking havoc.

title: How Batteries Got Cheaper and Made the Electric Grid More Reliable
content: An early grid battery was installed in the Atacama Desert in Chile 15 years ago. Now, as prices have tumbled, they are increasingly being used around the world.

title: Trump’s Relationship With the President of FIFA
content: Gianni Infantino, head of soccer’s governing body, FIFA, has lauded President Trump at almost every opportunity, even starting a FIFA Peace Prize after Mr. Trump didn’t win the Nobel. Luke Broadwater, a White House reporter, describes the bromance.

title: Trump Trumpets Peace in Africa Amid War on Drug Boats, in Day of Dissonance
content: President Trump presided over a Congo-Rwanda peace deal on the same day his administration was being questioned about potential war crimes.

title: Stellantis Is in Default for Moving Jeep Production to U.S., Canada Says
content: The automaker switched production from Ontario in a bid to please President Trump. But the company defaulted on contracts covering hundreds of millions of dollars in assistance, Canada said.

title: When Kids Adopt New Technologies, Hype Can Turn to Backlash
content: The arc of mobile phones and social media may foretell the future of artificial intelligence in schools.

title: Dominik Duka, Czech Cardinal Jailed Under Communism, Dies at 82
content: While in prison in 1981, he befriended the dissident and future Czech president Vaclav Havel. Later, he became a conservative voice in Rome.
